The Wool-Crowned Warrens

the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags started as a joke - a goblin sat on a llama once, on a dare - and now it's the closest thing this warren has to a government.

A sign of the floor's deeper story: Somewhere in the Larders, the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags is handing out promotions based entirely on who the llamas nuzzle first.

Tied to: Entrance (Room 0)

A sign of the floor's deeper story: the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags has turned the Larders into equal parts throne room and petting zoo, and nobody currently in charge can explain how that happened.

Tied to: Corridor Junction (Room 6)

This is where the floor's story comes to a head: the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags started as a joke - a goblin sat on a llama once, on a dare - and now it's the closest thing this warren has to a government. Its name is Corvin Blackwell, Drover of the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags. The stairs down to the next floor are here too - finding them means going through whatever's guarding this room first.

Tied to: Boss Arena (Room 28)
One llama has figured out that spitting on goblins gets it double rations, and has started training the others.
Two rival goblin chiefs have agreed to settle their feud with a llama race down the main hall - and both have been caught trying to bribe the same llama.
